Thanks for the details, Jared — and for the screenshot. Sorry for the friction here. A few quick things that often cause the behavior you describe:

- Corporate forwarding rules that rewrite the Return-Path or wrap the message can break invite tokens or cause our invites to be treated as internal redirect flows.
- Email security appliances that rewrite links/redirects for scanning sometimes change a Coupa PKI or signed header which can lead to invite-invalidation.

Can you do two quick checks so we can isolate:
1) Try opening the invite link in a private/incognito window (that avoids link-rewrite proxies in some browsers).
2) If you can, forward the raw full message (original headers) from your mail gateway to support@redwood.ai — that will let us see how the gateway rewrote things.

I've cc'd Ben (in infra) and Marissa (account lead) — Ben, can you look for any options to issue a one-time magic invite link or a token that bypasses the email flow? If not, I'll open a Coupa support ticket and request a non-redirecting URL.

I attached a short diagnostic template to capture the headers if Jared can paste them.

1) Issue a one-time, IP-restricted invite URL that is not tied to the original email token. I created a short-lived invite and pasted a masked link below — please try this from a browser on your corporate network and let me know the result.

That requires a short cooperation window with your IT to whitelist the Coupa IPs.

I've opened an official Coupa support ticket (INC-778341) and flagged it as high-priority for onboarding-blocking. Coupa support may also be able to provide an alternate entrypoint (SAML-redirect endpoint that tolerates rewritten URLs).
